title: In vitro and in vivo assay of the ER lipid scramblase TMEM41B
protocol: Reconstitute TMEM41B into liposomes for scramblase activity characterization using a fluorescence liposome-based in vitro assay.
Adapt trace amounts of 7-nitro-2-1,3-benzoxadiazol-4-yl acyl chain-labeled phosphatidylcholine (NBD-PC) to ∼50% distribution between the inner and outer leaflet of a symmetric liposome bilayer.
Add membrane-impermeant dithionite to quench outer leaflet NBD fluorescence of the liposomes, resulting in ∼50% fluorescence bleaching of NBD.
Observe greater fluorescent quenching due to exposure of inner leaflet NBD to dithionite on the outer leaflet in presence of scramblase (TMEM41B).
Wipe the table with 70% ethanol and ultraviolet irradiate for 30 min.
Expand FreeStyle™ 293F cells in 250 mL glass flasks in SMM 293-T1 medium supplemented with 0.5% Pen/strep and 1% FBS.
Incubate the cells at 37°C oscillation incubator with 5% CO2, optimal shaker speed of approximately 100–130 rpm.
Seed cells at 0.5 × 10^6 viable cells/mL when cell density reaches 2.0 × 10^6 viable cells/mL.
Transfect 1 μg plasmids per mL cells (DNA:PEI weight ratio of 3:1) when cell density is 1.5–2.0 × 10^6 viable cells/mL.
Dilute 50 μg plasmid DNA into 1.5 mL SMM 293-T1 medium and mix gently.
Incubate diluted DNA at RT (20°C–25°C) for 5 min.
Dilute 150 μg PEI into 1.5 mL SMM 293-T1 medium and mix gently.
Incubate diluted PEI at RT (20°C–25°C) for 5 min.
Mix the plasmid DNA with the PEI.
Incubate mixture of DNA-PEI complexes at RT (20°C–25°C) for 10–20 min.
Add mixture to 50 mL of cells and place in a 37°C oscillation incubator with 5% CO2.
Collect cells in 50 mL centrifuge tubes 48 hours after transfection.
Centrifuge at 1,000 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 10 mL of cold TBS buffer.
Centrifuge again at 1,000 g for another 10 minutes at 4°C.
Snap freeze the cell pellet in liquid nitrogen and store at -80°C until further use.
Thaw the cell pellet at 4°C.
Resuspend the thawed cells in 5 mL of buffer A containing DTT and protease inhibitor cocktail.
Lysis the suspension with a Dounce homogenizer (10 passes) to avoid protein degradation by minimizing bubble formation.
Add 0.5 mL of DDM stock solution to achieve a final concentration of 1% w/v, then gently rotate the mixture at 4°C for 90 minutes.
Transfer the lysate to an Open-Top Thinwall Polypropylene Tube and centrifuge at 100,000 g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and transfer it to a new 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Incubate the supernatant with 50 μL of ANTI-FLAG M2 beads at 4°C for 4 hours.
Pre-equilibrate ANTI-FLAG M2 beads with 1 mL buffer B in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the ANTI-FLAG M2 beads at 4,000 g for 1 min at 4°C to remove supernatant using Centrifuge 5424 R.
Repeat wash step three times.
Pellet the ANTI-FLAG M2 beads by centrifuging at 1,000 g for 10 min at 4°C in an Eppendorf 5810 R centrifuge with a 15 mL tube holder.
Transfer the ANTI-FLAG M2 beads to a new 1.5 mL tube.
Wash the beads with 1 mL buffer B about four times.

Incubate washed ANTI-FLAG M2 beads with 1 mL buffer B supplemented with 1 mM MgCl2, 2.5 mM ATP, and 1× EDTA-free Roche complete protease inhibitor cocktail at 4°C overnight (12–14 h) rotating at 10 rpm.
Wash the ANTI-FLAG M2 beads about six times with buffer B until the OD280 of the supernatant is close to 0, as detected by a NanoDrop 2000 Spectrophotometer.

Elute recombinant FLAG-TMEM41B protein from the ANTI-FLAG M2 beads using 500 μL of 0.1 mg/mL FLAG peptide in buffer B supplemented with 1× EDTA-free Roche complete protease inhibitor cocktail at 4°C for 2 h rotating at 10 rpm.
Concentrate eluted recombinant human FLAG-TMEM41B protein using Amicon 0.5 mL concentrators (10 kDa cutoffs) by centrifuging the concentrators at 10,000 g for 20 min at 4°C in Centrifuge 5424 R.
When liquid volume is reduced to a fifth of its original amount, add 450 μL buffer B.
Repeat the buffer change step for human FLAG-TMEM41B protein three times using buffer B.
Concentrate the volume of the protein to 50–100 μL after each buffer exchange.
Dilute BSA protein from Pierce™ BCA Protein Detection Kit in a series of concentrations (1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, 1/32 and 1/64 mg/mL) for use as standards.
Load the same volume of purified human FLAG-TMEM41B and BSA protein onto SDS-PAGE gel.
Dissolve POPC, POPG, and NBD-PC in chloroform on ice to achieve final concentrations of 25 mg/mL, 25 mg/mL, and 1 mg/mL respectively.
Add 143.5 μL POPC, 16 μL POPG and 9.5 μL NBD-PC (about 0.2 mol% of total phospholipids) to a 100 mL bottle.
Dry the lipids by rotary evaporation under an argon or nitrogen stream at 120 rpm for 5–15 min until chloroform evaporates.
Transfer the flask to a vacuum desiccator at room temperature (20°C-25°C) for at least 3 h or overnight.
Resuspend the lipid film in 0.5 mL buffer C by gently swirling the flask and incubate at 37°C for 10 min until forming a homogenous turbid solution.
Transfer the lipid solution to a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Freeze-thaw the MLVs for 10 cycles by alternately placing it in liquid nitrogen and at a 37°C water bath.
Extrude the lipids suspension 20 times through a membrane with a 400 nm pore size.
Extrude the samples 10 times through a membrane with a 200 nm pore size at room temperature (RT).
Transfer the extruded samples to a new 2 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Store the liposomes at 4°C and use within the day of preparation.
Dilute the liposomes in buffer C to a final lipids concentration of 5.25 mM (∼3.98 mg/mL).
Add Triton X-100 to the liposomes to a final concentration of 7 mM.
Rotate (10 rpm) at RT for 2–3 h to destabilize the liposomes.
Incubate the solution with 7 mM Triton X-100 to destabilize liposomes particles.
After 2-3 hours of incubation, add 0.2% (w/v) DDM-solubilized recombinant human FLAG-TMEM41B protein (∼0.1 mg/mL) to the samples.
Gently rotate the mixture at 10 rpm and room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 1 hour.
Wash bio-beads twice with methanol, three times with ddH2O, and once with buffer C.
Stir each washing solution slowly for 10 minutes during washing steps.
Prepare 100 mg of bio-beads for each sample, which can be prepared in bulk if needed.
Add 20 mg of the prepared bio-beads to each sample.
Rotate the mixture at 10 rpm and room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 1 hour.
After initial incubation with bio-beads, add an additional 20 mg of bio-beads to each sample.
Rotate the mixture at 10 rpm and room temperature (20°C–25°C) for another 2 hours.
Transfer the liquid by gel loading tips to a new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube containing 40 mg of fresh bio-beads and rotate (10 rpm) at 4°C overnight (12–14 h).
Transfer the sample to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube with a hole in the lid.
Cover the hole with a pre-washed dialysis membrane (30 kDa).
Close the lid and ensure no leakage.
Put the lid under liquid in a 500 mL beaker containing buffer C, stir using a magnetic rotor at 150 rpm.
Dialyze against buffer C at 4°C for 2 days to remove remaining detergent.
Ensure dialysis membrane and microcentrifuge tube cover lid are tightly closed to prevent fluid leakage.
Keep the solution from light after incubation with bio-beads and dialysis.
Monitor NBD fluorescence per sample using Gen5™ software in the Synergy H1 Hybrid Multi-Mode Reader.
Record fluorescence with an inspection interval of 10 seconds for approximately 200 seconds.
Dissolve 1 mg of dithionite in 57 μL ice-cold 0.5 M Tris immediately before use and keep on ice.
Add 10 mM dithionite to monitor the reduction of NBD fluorescence after ∼600 seconds recording.
Record data for approximately 600 seconds post-dithionite addition.
Add 2.5 μL of 20% (w/v) Triton X-100 to each sample to destabilize liposomes/proteoliposomes and completely bleach NBD fluorescence.
Calculate the relative fluorescent intensity according to the formula FI(t)/FI(0) = [Ft - F Triton] / [F0 - F Triton].
Perform cell-related operations in a Class II biological safety cabinet.
Wipe the table with 70% ethanol.
Ultraviolet irradiate the workspace for 30 minutes.
Seed WT and CRISPR/Cas9-mediated TMEM41B knockout Huh7 cells on Fisherbrand™ Borosilicate Glass Square Coverslip in 6-well Cell Culture plates at ∼25% confluence.
After 12 hours, transfect each well with 1 μg GFP-SEC61β plasmids.
Mix 1 μg GFP-SEC61β plasmids with 200 μL serum-free DMEM and incubate at RT for 5 minutes.
Add 4 μg PEI to the mixture, mix gently, and incubate at RT for 15 minutes.
After incubation, add the transfection medium to the cells.
8 hours after transfection, exchange media with DMEM supplemented with 1% Pen/strep, 10% FBS, and 100 μM alkyne-choline.
Culture the cells for another 12–24 hours.
Wash cells with 1× PBS three times.
Fix cells with 4% (w/v) formaldehyde at RT for 15 minutes.
Wash cells with 1× PBS three times.
Permeabilize cells with 25 μg/mL digitonin in 1× PBS for 10 minutes.
Wash cells with PBS three times.
Incubate cells on coverslips with 10 μM 5-TAMRA azide, BTTAA-CuSO4 complex (50 μM CuSO4), and 2.5 mM sodium ascorbate in 1× PBS at RT for 1 hour.
Prepare 200 μL click reaction mixture immediately before use.
Wash cells with 1× PBS three times, 10 minutes each time.
Block cells in 1× PBS with 1% BSA at RT for 15 minutes.
Mount coverslips to a glass slide and allow mounting medium to dry.
Optionally seal slides with colorless nail polish.
Subject prepared samples to confocal microscopy using Zeiss LSM 880 with Airyscan confocal microscope.
Capture images of GFP and TAMRA channels visualizing ER (SEC61β) and PC (alkyne-choline), respectively, at specified parameters.
Save captured images as LSM files with a resolution of 1024 × 1024.
Open LSM files in ImageJ Fiji for analysis.
Crop images to select the region on the periphery of the ER using selection tools.
From the Analyze menu select “Set Measurements”.
Make sure area integrated intensity and mean gray value are selected.
Select “Measure” from the Analyze menu.
Select a region next to your cell that has no fluorescence.
Take this as the background signal.
Subtract the value of the target area from the value of the background area.
Open the LSM files by ImageJ Fiji.
Crop images to select a region of interest using the selection tool.
From the Image menu select “Color-Split Channels” to divide pictures into different channels.
Select “Colocalization-Coloc 2” from the analyze menu for colocalization analysis.
Analyze data difference from TMEM41B WT and KO Huh7 cells using GraphPad Prism8.
Use a two-tailed Student’s t-test to compare data differences.
Quantify the fluorescent intensity of periphery ER (GFP-SEC61β) in the TAMRA channel for both TMEM41B WT and KO cells.
